- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next period to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.36) and price is trending up, model often overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or mean of last 5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.18–0.36) and price is volatile, model exhibits lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- If model consistently forecasts below true outcome (especially in early horizon), it may be missing sentiment-driven momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.30.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if price deviates >3% from 10-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average with sentiment as weighting factor.
